Aposematic coloration (A) and chemical defenses (B) are directly evolved to deter natural enemies.  
Masting (C) is a predator satiation strategy — producing so many seeds at once that predators can’t eat them all — so it is driven by natural enemies.  
Lekking behavior (D) is a mating system in which males gather for competitive displays to attract females; it’s driven by sexual selection, not directly by natural enemies.  

Final answer: (D)
